headline: Cohere, a Canadian AI company, has launched North 2, a new version of its platform that lets large organisations run AI agents with memory and cap what they spend.
score_reason: Pool score lowered two points: the launch was on 5 Oct 2026, we carried it on 6 Oct 2026, and nothing new is reported today.
importance_line: Administrators and staff at large organisations get tools to cap what AI agents cost and to limit what they may do, but the claims are Cohere's own, no prices or independent tests are given, and the news is five days old.
summary: SiliconANGLE reported on 5 Oct 2026 that Cohere unveiled North 2, an overhaul of its platform for running AI agents (software that carries out multistep tasks on its own) in which agents keep a memory between sessions, can be shared across a company and pass steps that need sign-off to a person, while an admin console tracks token use (the units in which AI models measure and bill their work) by user and agent and lets administrators set spending caps. We carried this in our 6 Oct 2026 edition, and today's Chinese-language write-up on Zhiding repeats the same details rather than adding anything new.
notes: REPEAT of 6 Oct 2026 edition item 89 (same SiliconANGLE URL); recommend dropping at the no-old-news check. The pool's Zhiding text was garbled, so the original SiliconANGLE report was read directly; Quasa.io (8 Oct 2026) confirms the 5 Oct launch and cites Cohere, The Register and VentureBeat.
